import Callout from "../../../components/docs/Callout.astro";

A theme is a folder with a manifest and a stylesheet. This guide creates a complete theme, installs it from the settings, and checks both modes.

## 1. Create the folder

```text
midnight-blurple/
├── manifest.json
└── theme.css
```

The folder name does not have to match the id for a local theme, but the id becomes the installed folder name. Keep them identical to avoid duplicate-id confusion.

## 2. Write the manifest

```json
{
  "id": "midnight-blurple",
  "name": "Midnight Blurple",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "author": "Your name",
  "description": "Cool blues on a deep navy base.",
  "license": "MIT",
  "mode": "both",
  "tags": ["dark", "blue"],
  "api": 1,
  "css": "theme.css"
}
```

`id` and `name` are the required identity fields. `api` is optional but should be `1` for the current format. `mode` is `dark`, `light` or `both`; `both` follows the app's mode setting, which can follow the system.

The manifest reference covers every field and the exact file rules: [Structure and manifest](/yapmod/docs/themes/manifest).

## 3. Write the stylesheet

```css
/* theme.css */

:root[data-yapmod-mode="dark"] {
  --ym-bg-rail: #101116;
  --ym-bg-side: #16171e;
  --ym-bg-main: #1b1c23;
  --ym-bg-elev: #22232c;
  --ym-bg-hover: #292a34;
  --ym-bg-active: #33343f;
  --ym-text: #ececf1;
  --ym-text-muted: #9c9daa;
  --ym-border: #ffffff14;
  --ym-accent: #5865f2;
  --ym-accent-soft: #5865f233;
  --ym-on-accent: #ffffff;
  --ym-radius: 10px;
}

:root[data-yapmod-mode="light"] {
  --ym-bg-rail: #e3e5e8;
  --ym-bg-side: #f2f3f5;
  --ym-bg-main: #ffffff;
  --ym-bg-elev: #ebedef;
  --ym-bg-hover: #e6e7ea;
  --ym-bg-active: #d7d9de;
  --ym-text: #1d1f23;
  --ym-text-muted: #5b5d66;
  --ym-border: #00000017;
  --ym-accent: #5865f2;
  --ym-accent-soft: #5865f224;
  --ym-on-accent: #ffffff;
  --ym-radius: 10px;
}
```

The `--ym-*` tokens are yapmod's stable names. The token layer maps the ones you set onto the app's own variables. You do not need to touch every token; a missing token keeps the value from the generated token layer.

Browse the full generated list on [Styling and tokens](/yapmod/docs/themes/styling).

## 4. Install it

1. Open **Settings → Themes** in yapmod.
2. Choose **Import theme** and select the theme folder.
3. Confirm that the theme appears in the Installed gallery.
4. Pick it. The change is immediate and remembered.

Alternatively, press **Open folder**, copy the theme folder into the themes directory, and press **Refresh**. Import is safer because it copies the folder for you and rejects a duplicate id.

An imported theme is copied under its id. To import an updated version of the same theme, remove the installed theme first.

## 5. Test both modes

If the theme declares `"mode": "both"`, use the **Mode** control in the theme settings to switch between following the system, dark and light. Confirm that:

- every token you set has a sensible value in both blocks;
- text remains readable on every surface;
- borders remain visible;
- the accent and `--ym-on-accent` have sufficient contrast;
- dialogs, popovers and hover states are still legible.

If the theme is dark-only or light-only, set `mode` accordingly. A one-mode theme does not need a second token block, and the app will keep that mode while the theme is active.

## 6. Recover safely

A theme is plain CSS and can break the layout. If the interface becomes unusable:

1. Open **Settings → Themes** if it is still visible.
2. Pick **Yapper's theme** to restore the normal look.
3. Remove the broken theme with the × on its card.

There is no JavaScript in a theme, so removing it is enough; there is no background code to stop.

<Callout type="tip" title="Start with tokens, then add CSS">
A theme built only from tokens is portable across app updates. Add component-specific rules after the token layer looks right, and keep those rules narrow.
</Callout>
